method: lattice preserved; only view-axis atom coordinates degraded; spglib symprec 1e-2; stratified 6/system x 3 axis views = 126 measurements per set
branch: MIXED - D3 on original (helps only box-sufficient, ambiguous 0.2381->0.2381), D1 on expansion (ambiguous doubles 0.1282->0.2564). Third render-related split across these two samples.
ceiling: even at 16 levels, box-ambiguous recovery is 0.2564 vs 1.0000 with full depth: ordinal depth closes at most ~13 of ~75 available points

rank_variant_defect.cause: uniform rank spacing is a NONLINEAR DISTORTION along the view axis; it moves atoms to positions they do not occupy and destroys metric relations a flat projection leaves intact. It measured the harm of a distortion, not the value of an added cue.
rank_variant_defect.detection: R < P is incoherent for a variant that supposedly ADDS information
rank_variant_defect.design_warning: an ordinal depth cue interpreted as evenly spaced is WORSE than no depth cue; depth grading must be metric-faithful, not merely monotone

recommendation: do NOT commission Stage 1 as an accuracy intervention; keep Q4-saturation and metric-faithfulness as free render-design observations
limits: perfect atom localisation assumed, as in the oracle; bounds what depth COULD carry given extraction, not what any model reads

quantization_saturation_per_stratum.note: expansion/box_sufficient gains 0.0115 (1 of 87 measurements) between Q4 and Q8 and only then flattens, so the across-strata saturation point is 8. An earlier version hard-coded 4 and licensed 'four levels is enough', which its own per-stratum data contradicted.

paired_quantization_tests_pooled.conclusion: BOTH steps significant - no saturation at 4 or 8 within the tested range; the earlier flatness was a low-power artifact of a 252-measurement subsample

correction_history: claim stated 3x and wrong each time: 'saturates at 4' (subsample, self-contradictory), corrected to 'by 8' after review, now WITHDRAWN once powered at 1260 measurements. No level-count recommendation is shipped.
